svg.title: Hold the requests back, then multiply once
svg.desc: Blank version of the sketch “Hold the requests back, then multiply once” with all labels removed, for drawing from memory. On the left eight arriving requests each get their own 23-millisecond forward pass at p99 94 milliseconds and 156 requests per second; on the right the same eight are held in a five-millisecond batch window and run as one 31-millisecond pass at p99 78 and 289 rps, with 5.9 times fewer kernel launches; below, a three-by-three grid of measured throughput and p99 for two serving stacks at batch sizes one, eight and thirty-two with the batch-32 TF Serving cell circled at 2.3x, payload bars for REST JSON, gRPC and base64 JPEG, and a shadow-traffic sketch.
svg.text: Hold the requests back, then multiply once
draw it from memory, then compare
